helpful: Provisioned petition and BIO as full text made the vehicle analysis possible; the BIO's citations to the state-court briefs were the most decision-relevant material.
The sal-v4 band table's bracketed reached figures gave a clean pooled anchor.
CourtListener opinion search confirmed the post-petition Anash decision in one call.
gaps: No statpack cut for 'response requested after waiver', which is the strongest docket signal on this petition and had to be weighted by judgment.
fedcourts query has no subject or statute filter, so it cannot retrieve RLUIPA priors; the four prior RLUIPA land-use denials had to come from the parties' own citations.
The reply brief and the amicus briefs were not provisioned; the reply's treatment of Anash and the vehicle arguments would have sharpened the number.
CourtListener docket search did not resolve SCOTUS docket numbers (25-965), so related SCOTUS dockets were only reachable through the corpus data tree.
notes: The corpus query's 3 MB ranged read for five generic rows is expensive relative to its value on a cert cell; a subject filter would make it worth the egress.
